items.title: Natty Dominique Interview, 1967-11-15
items.q: I was standing right alongside Baby Dots, looking at that music.

ctx.x: So, I said, Ben, what do you want to play? I said, Duke, what are you going to play? I can't play no numbers. He said, just play in the numbers. He said, I'll play some. He picked up a number. So, I told Dave, I said, oh, Dave, you don't want no music to hear? He said, no. He said, no. And here's Dave, that's here. I always put him on there. Here's Sonny Gray on. Here's this side. Look at that. Look at that. That's that drummer that the government. So, man, we struck up. I made a double-fought introduction. Loud.…
I thought he played that Spanish number. Duke. I was standing right alongside Baby Dots, looking at that music. He said, now, if I could get that man, I'd be on top of the world.

I said, well, they're two brothers, they're together. I said, I can't stop him. I don't give him. But he could have went the next day. Because if he just said, yeah, you want to go, I wouldn't accept for two weeks. I said, go on. I let him go. It's like going on Hawkins. You know what that band New York? They had to mainly kick him out of the band. Make him go to England. Coleman Hawkins, you know what you're talking about in that saxophone play tennis sax? Yeah. Great. He don't put no more than this, look. And…

items.title: Natty Dominique Interview, 1958-05-31
items.q: Cause there's nobody like Baby Dots. Baby Dots. Baby Dots. I still say. I take my boy.

ctx.x: That's a beautiful. That's. Don't. Cause there's nobody like Baby Dots. Baby Dots. Baby Dots. I still say. I take my boy. I'm not mad at him.
